questions.q: $n^{th}$ term of the series $1 + \dfrac{3}{7} + \dfrac{5}{7^2} + \dfrac{7}{7^3} + \cdots$ is
questions.explanation: The $n^{th}$ term is $\dfrac{2n-1}{7^{n-1}}$: check $n=1$ gives $1$, $n=2$ gives $3/7$, $n=3$ gives $5/49$, matching the series.

questions.q: If $p\left(\dfrac{1}{q}+\dfrac{1}{r}\right), q\left(\dfrac{1}{r}+\dfrac{1}{p}\right), r\left(\dfrac{1}{p}+\dfrac{1}{q}\right)$ are in A.P., then p, q, r
questions.explanation: Testing $p,q,r$ in A.P. (e.g. $1,2,3$) makes the three given expressions have equal common difference, so the condition forces $p,q,r$ to be in A.P.

questions.q: A line passes through $(2, 2)$ and is perpendicular to the line $3x + y = 3$. Its y-intercept is
questions.explanation: Slope of $3x+y=3$ is $-3$, so perpendicular slope is $1/3$. Line: $y-2=\dfrac{1}{3}(x-2)$, giving y-intercept $= 2-\dfrac{2}{3}=\dfrac{4}{3}$.

questions.q: The distance between the foci of a hyperbola is 16 and its eccentricity is $\sqrt{2}$. Its equation is
questions.explanation: $2c=16 \Rightarrow c=8$; $e=\sqrt2 \Rightarrow a = c/e = 4\sqrt2 \Rightarrow a^2=32$; $b^2=c^2-a^2=32$. Equation: $x^2-y^2=32$.

questions.q: If $\displaystyle\lim_{x \to 0} \dfrac{\sin(2+x) - \sin(2-x)}{x} = A \cos B$, then the values of A and B respectively are
questions.explanation: $\sin(2+x)-\sin(2-x) = 2\cos 2 \sin x$, so the limit $= 2\cos2 \cdot \lim \dfrac{\sin x}{x} = 2\cos2$. So $A=2, B=2$.

questions.q: If n is even and the middle term in the expansion of $\left(x^2 + \dfrac{1}{x}\right)^n$ is $924x^6$, then n is equal to
questions.explanation: Middle term (r = n/2) has exponent of x equal to $2n-3r = n/2$. Setting $n/2 = 6$ gives $n=12$, and $\binom{12}{6}=924$ confirms it.

questions.q: The mean of 100 observations is 50 and their standard deviation is 5. Then the sum of squares of all observations is
$f : R \to R$ and $g : [0, \infty) \to R$ are defined by $f(x) = x^2$ and $g(x) = \sqrt{x}$. Which one of the following is not true?
questions.explanation: $g$ has domain $[0,\infty)$, so $g(-4)$ is undefined; hence $(fog)(-4)$ cannot equal 4 — the other three statements check out directly.

questions.q: Let $f : R \to R$ be defined by $f(x) = 3x^2 - 5$ and $g : R \to R$ by $g(x) = \dfrac{x}{x^2+1}$, then gof is
Let the relation R be defined in N by aRb if $3a + 2b = 27$, then R is
questions.explanation: Solving $3a+2b=27$ for $a,b \in N$ (positive integers) gives pairs $(1,12),(3,9),(5,6),(7,3)$ — $a=9$ would force $b=0 \notin N$.

questions.q: Let $f(x) = \sin 2x + \cos 2x$ and $g(x) = x^2 - 1$, then $g(f(x))$ is invertible in the domain
questions.explanation: $g(f(x)) = (\sin2x+\cos2x)^2-1 = \sin4x$, which is one-one (invertible) on $\left[\dfrac{-\pi}{8},\dfrac{\pi}{8}\right]$ where $4x \in \left[\dfrac{-\pi}{2},\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right]$.

questions.q: The contrapositive of the statement "If two lines do not intersect in the same plane then they are parallel." is
options: If two lines are not parallel then they do not intersect in the same plane.
If two lines are not parallel then they intersect in the same plane.
If two lines are parallel then they do not intersect in the same plane.
If two lines are parallel then they intersect in the same plane.
questions.explanation: Contrapositive of \"if p then q\" is \"if not q then not p\": negating \"parallel\" and \"do not intersect\" and swapping gives \"If two lines are not parallel then they intersect in the same plane.\"

questions.q: The value of $\cot^{-1}\left[\dfrac{\sqrt{1-\sin x}+\sqrt{1+\sin x}}{\sqrt{1-\sin x}-\sqrt{1+\sin x}}\right]$ where $x \in \left(0, \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right)$ is
questions.explanation: Using $1\pm\sin x = (\cos(x/2)\pm\sin(x/2))^2$, the fraction simplifies to $-\cot(x/2)$, and $\cot^{-1}(-\cot(x/2)) = \pi - \dfrac{x}{2}$.

questions.q: If $x\begin{bmatrix}3\\2\end{bmatrix} + y\begin{bmatrix}1\\-1\end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix}15\\5\end{bmatrix}$ then the value of x and y are
questions.explanation: $3x+y=15$ and $2x-y=5$. Adding: $5x=20 \Rightarrow x=4$, then $y=15-12=3$.

questions.q: If A and B are two matrices such that $AB = B$ and $BA = A$ then $A^2 + B^2 =$
questions.explanation: $A^2 = A(BA) = (AB)A = BA = A$, and similarly $B^2 = B(AB) = (BA)B = AB = B$. So $A^2+B^2 = A+B$.

questions.q: If $A = \begin{bmatrix}2-k & 2\\1 & 3-k\end{bmatrix}$ is a singular matrix, then the value of $5k - k^2$ is equal to
questions.explanation: $|A|=0 \Rightarrow (2-k)(3-k)-2=0 \Rightarrow k^2-5k+4=0 \Rightarrow k^2-5k=-4$. So $5k-k^2 = 4$.

questions.q: The area of a triangle with vertices $(-3, 0), (3, 0)$ and $(0, k)$ is 9 sq. units, the value of k is
questions.explanation: Area $= \dfrac{1}{2}\times \text{base}(6) \times |k| = 3|k| = 9 \Rightarrow k = 3$.

questions.q: If $\Delta = \begin{vmatrix}1 & a & a^2\\1 & b & b^2\\1 & c & c^2\end{vmatrix}$ and $\Delta_1 = \begin{vmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\bc & ca & ab\\a & b & c\end{vmatrix}$ then
questions.explanation: Testing $a=1,b=2,c=3$ gives $\Delta=2$ and $\Delta_1=-2$, so $\Delta_1 = -\Delta$ (a standard determinant identity).

questions.q: If $\sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2a}{1+a^2}\right) + \cos^{-1}\left(\dfrac{1-a^2}{1+a^2}\right) = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)$ where $a, x \in (0, 1)$ then the value of x is
questions.explanation: Both terms on the left equal $2\tan^{-1}a$, so LHS $=4\tan^{-1}a = 2\tan^{-1}x$, giving $\tan^{-1}x = 2\tan^{-1}a$ and $x = \dfrac{2a}{1-a^2}$.

questions.q: If $u = \sin^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1+x^2}\right)$ and $v = \tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2x}{1-x^2}\right)$ then $\dfrac{du}{dv}$ is
questions.explanation: For $|x|<1$, both $u$ and $v$ equal $2\tan^{-1}x$, so $u=v$ and $\dfrac{du}{dv}=1$.

questions.q: The function $f(x) = \cot x$ is discontinuous on every point of the set
questions.explanation: $\cot x = \cos x/\sin x$ is undefined wherever $\sin x = 0$, i.e. at $x = n\pi,\ n \in Z$.

questions.q: If the function is $f(x) = \dfrac{1}{x+2}$, then the point of discontinuity of the composite function $y = f(f(x))$ is
questions.explanation: $f(f(x)) = \dfrac{x+2}{2x+5}$, which is discontinuous at $x=-5/2$ (also at $x=-2$, not listed).

questions.q: If $y = a \sin x + b \cos x$, then $y^2 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$ is a
questions.explanation: $y^2+(y')^2 = (a\sin x+b\cos x)^2+(a\cos x-b\sin x)^2 = a^2+b^2$, a constant.

questions.q: If $f(x) = 1 + nx + \dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}x^2 + \dfrac{n(n-1)(n-2)}{6}x^3 + \cdots + x^n$ then $f''(1) =$
If $A = \begin{bmatrix}1 & \tan(\alpha/2)\\-\tan(\alpha/2) & 1\end{bmatrix}$ and $AB = I$ then $B =$
questions.explanation: $AA^T = \sec^2(\alpha/2) I$, so $A^{-1} = \cos^2(\alpha/2) A^T$; since $AB=I$, $B = A^{-1} = \cos^2(\alpha/2) A^T$.

questions.q: A circular plate of radius 5 cm is heated. Due to expansion, its radius increases at the rate of 0.05 cm/sec. The rate at which its area is increasing when the radius is 5.2 cm is
questions.explanation: $A=\pi r^2 \Rightarrow \dfrac{dA}{dt} = 2\pi r \dfrac{dr}{dt} = 2\pi(5.2)(0.05) = 0.52\pi$ cm$^2$/sec.

questions.q: The distance 's' in meters travelled by a particle in 't' seconds is given by $s = \dfrac{2t^3}{3} - 18t + \dfrac{5}{3}$. The acceleration when the particle comes to rest is
questions.explanation: $v = 2t^2-18 = 0 \Rightarrow t=3$ (rest). $a = 4t = 12$ m/sec$^2$.

questions.q: A particle moves along the curve $\dfrac{x^2}{16} + \dfrac{y^2}{4} = 1$. When the rate of change of abscissa is 4 times that of its ordinate, then the quadrant in which the particle lies is
questions.explanation: Differentiating and substituting $dx/dt = 4\,dy/dt$ gives $x+y=0$, i.e. $y=-x$; on the ellipse this occurs in quadrants II and IV.

questions.q: An enemy fighter jet is flying along the curve given by $y = x^2 + 2$. A soldier is placed at $(3, 2)$ wants to shoot down the jet when it is nearest to him. Then the nearest distance is
questions.explanation: Minimizing $D^2=(x-3)^2+x^4$ gives $2x^3+x-3=0$ with root $x=1$, point $(1,3)$; distance $=\sqrt{(1-3)^2+(3-2)^2}=\sqrt5$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{2}^{8} \dfrac{5^{\sqrt{10-x}}}{5^{\sqrt x}+5^{\sqrt{10-x}}}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: Using $\int_a^b f(x)dx = \int_a^b f(a+b-x)dx$ with $a+b=10$, adding the original and transformed integrals gives $2I = 6$, so $I=3$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \sqrt{\csc x - \sin x}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: $\csc x-\sin x = \dfrac{\cos^2x}{\sin x}$, so $\sqrt{\csc x-\sin x} = \dfrac{\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin x}}$, and $\int \dfrac{\cos x}{\sqrt{\sin x}}dx = 2\sqrt{\sin x}+C$.

questions.q: If $f(x)$ and $g(x)$ are two functions with $g(x) = x - \dfrac{1}{x}$ and $fog(x) = x^3 - \dfrac{1}{x^3}$ then $f'(x) =$
questions.explanation: Since $x^3-1/x^3 = t^3+3t$ where $t=x-1/x$, we get $f(t)=t^3+3t$, so $f(x)=x^3+3x$ and $f'(x)=3x^2+3$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \dfrac{1}{1 + 3\sin^2 x + 8\cos^2 x}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: Dividing numerator and denominator by $\cos^2x$ gives $\int \dfrac{\sec^2x}{9+4\tan^2x}dx = \dfrac{1}{6}\tan^{-1}\left(\dfrac{2\tan x}{3}\right)+C$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0} \left(x^3 + 3x^2 + 3x + 3 + (x+1)\cos(x+1)\right)\,dx =$
questions.explanation: Substituting $u=x+1$ (limits $-1$ to $1$): $x^3+3x^2+3x+3=(x+1)^3+2=u^3+2$, so integrand $=u^3+2+u\cos u$; the odd parts vanish over $[-1,1]$, leaving $\int_{-1}^1 2\,du = 4$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int_{0}^{\pi} \dfrac{x\tan x}{\sec x \cdot \csc x}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{\tan x}{\sec x \csc x} = \sin^2x$; using $\int_0^a x f(x)dx=\dfrac{a}{2}\int_0^a f(x)dx$ (since $\sin^2(\pi-x)=\sin^2x$), $I=\dfrac{\pi}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\pi}{2}=\pi^2/4$.

questions.q: $\displaystyle\int \sqrt{5 - 2x + x^2}\,dx =$
questions.explanation: With $x^2-2x+5=(x-1)^2+4$, the standard formula $\int\sqrt{t^2+a^2}dt$ gives $\dfrac{x-1}{2}\sqrt{5-2x+x^2}+2\log|(x-1)+\sqrt{5-2x+x^2}|+C$.

If a curve passes through the point $(1, 1)$ and at any point $(x, y)$ on the curve, the product of the slope of its tangent and x co-ordinate of the point is equal to the y co-ordinate of the point, then the curve also passes through the point
questions.explanation: $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y \Rightarrow y=kx$; through $(1,1)$, $k=1$ so $y=x$, which passes through $(2,2)$.

questions.q: The degree of the differential equation $1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2 = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+1}$ is
questions.explanation: Cubing both sides to remove the cube root gives a polynomial equation in which the highest-order derivative $d^2y/dx^2$ appears with power 6, so the degree is 6.

questions.q: If $|\vec a + \vec b| = |\vec a - \vec b|$ then
questions.explanation: Squaring both sides gives $\vec a \cdot \vec b = 0$, so $\vec a$ and $\vec b$ are perpendicular.

questions.q: The component of $\hat i$ in the direction of the vector $\hat i + \hat j + 2\hat k$ is
questions.explanation: Component $= \dfrac{\hat i \cdot (\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k)}{|\hat i+\hat j+2\hat k|} = \dfrac{1}{\sqrt6} = \dfrac{\sqrt6}{6}$.

questions.q: In the interval $(0, \pi/2)$, area lying between the curves $y = \tan x$ and $y = \cot x$ and the X-axis is
questions.explanation: The curves meet at $x=\pi/4$; area $=\int_0^{\pi/4}\tan x\,dx+\int_{\pi/4}^{\pi/2}\cot x\,dx = \dfrac12\ln2+\dfrac12\ln2=\ln2$.

questions.q: If $\vec a + 2\vec b + 3\vec c = \vec 0$ and $(\vec a \times \vec b) + (\vec b \times \vec c) + (\vec c \times \vec a) = \lambda(\vec b \times \vec c)$ then the value of $\lambda$ is equal to
questions.explanation: With $\vec a = -2\vec b-3\vec c$: $\vec a\times\vec b=3(\vec b\times\vec c)$ and $\vec c\times\vec a=2(\vec b\times\vec c)$, so the sum $=6(\vec b\times\vec c)$, giving $\lambda=6$.

questions.q: If a line makes an angle of $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ with each X and Y axis then the acute angle made by Z-axis is
questions.explanation: $\cos^2\alpha+\cos^2\beta+\cos^2\gamma=1$ with $\alpha=\beta=\pi/3$ gives $\cos^2\gamma=1/2$, so $\gamma=\pi/4$.

questions.q: The length of perpendicular drawn from the point $(3, -1, 11)$ to the line $\dfrac{x}{2} = \dfrac{y-2}{3} = \dfrac{z-3}{4}$ is
questions.explanation: Using $d = \dfrac{|\vec{AP}\times\vec d|}{|\vec d|}$ with $\vec{AP}=(3,-3,8)$ and $\vec d=(2,3,4)$ gives $d=\sqrt{1537/29}=\sqrt{53}$.

questions.q: The equation of the plane through the points $(2, 1, 0), (3, 2, -2)$ and $(3, 1, 7)$ is
The point of intersection of the line $x + 1 = \dfrac{y+3}{3} = \dfrac{-z+2}{2}$ with the plane $3x + 4y + 5z = 10$ is
questions.explanation: Parametrize $x=-1+t, y=-3+3t, z=2-2t$; substituting into the plane gives $t=3$, so the point is $(2,6,-4)$.

questions.q: If $(2, 3, -1)$ is the foot of the perpendicular from $(4, 2, 1)$ to a plane, then the equation of the plane is
If $|\vec a \times \vec b|^2 + |\vec a \cdot \vec b|^2 = 144$ and $|\vec a| = 4$ then $|\vec b|$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Using $|\vec a\times\vec b|^2+|\vec a\cdot\vec b|^2=|\vec a|^2|\vec b|^2$, we get $16|\vec b|^2=144 \Rightarrow |\vec b|=3$.

questions.q: If A and B are events such that $P(A) = \dfrac{1}{4}$, $P(A/B) = \dfrac{1}{2}$ and $P(B/A) = \dfrac{2}{3}$ then P(B) is
questions.explanation: $P(A\cap B)=P(B/A)P(A)=\dfrac23\cdot\dfrac14=\dfrac16$; $P(B)=\dfrac{P(A\cap B)}{P(A/B)}=\dfrac{1/6}{1/2}=\dfrac13$.

questions.q: A bag contains $2n + 1$ coins. It is known that n of these coins have head on both sides whereas the other $n + 1$ coins are fair. One coin is selected at random and tossed. If the probability that toss results in heads is $\dfrac{31}{42}$, then the value of n is
questions.explanation: $P(\text{head}) = \dfrac{n\cdot1+(n+1)\cdot\frac12}{2n+1} = \dfrac{3n+1}{2(2n+1)} = \dfrac{31}{42}$, solving gives $n=10$.

questions.q: Let $A = \{x, y, z, u\}$ and $B = \{a, b\}$. A function $f : A \to B$ is selected randomly. The probability that the function is an onto function is
questions.explanation: Total functions $=2^4=16$; onto functions $=2^4-2=14$ (excluding the 2 constant maps); probability $=14/16=7/8$.

questions.q: The shaded region in the figure given is the solution of which of the inequations? [Figure: a shaded triangle with vertices A(7,0), B(3,4) and C(0,2), bounded by the line through (0,7) and (7,0) i.e. $x+y=7$, and the line through (-3,0) and (3,4) i.e. $2x-3y+6=0$, lying in the first quadrant]
questions.explanation: Testing the centroid $(10/3, 2)$ of the shaded triangle satisfies $x+y\le7$ and $2x-3y+6\ge0$, along with $x,y\ge0$.

questions.q: If $f(x) = ax + b$, where a and b are integers, $f(-1) = -5$ and $f(3) = 3$, then a and b respectively are
questions.explanation: $-a+b=-5$ and $3a+b=3$; subtracting gives $4a=8 \Rightarrow a=2$, then $b=-3$.

questions.q: The value of $e^{\log_{10}\tan1° + \log_{10}\tan2° + \log_{10}\tan3° + \cdots + \log_{10}\tan89°}$ is
questions.explanation: The sum of logs equals $\log_{10}(\tan1°\tan2°\cdots\tan89°) = \log_{10}1 = 0$ (pairing $\tan\theta\cdot\tan(90°-\theta)=1$), so $e^0=1$.

questions.q: The value of $\begin{vmatrix}\sin^2 14° & \sin^2 66° & \tan 135°\\sin^2 66° & \tan 135° & \sin^2 14°\\tan 135° & \sin^2 14° & \sin^2 66°\end{vmatrix}$ is
questions.note: With a=sin$^2$14°, b=sin$^2$66°, c=tan135°=-1, the determinant equals -(a+b+c)(a$^2$+b$^2$+c$^2$-ab-bc-ca), which is exactly 0 only if a+b+c=0, i.e. sin$^2$14°+sin$^2$66°=1. That identity actually holds for complementary angles summing to 90° (e.g. 24°+66°), not 14°+66°=80°; numerically the determinant with the printed 14° is $\approx$0.27, matching no option. This looks like a printing error for 24° (which would make the identity exact and give 0); KEA's key credits 0.
questions.explanation: Writing a=sin$^2$14°, b=sin$^2$66°, c=tan135°=-1, the determinant equals $3abc-(a^3+b^3+c^3)=-(a+b+c)(a^2+b^2+c^2-ab-bc-ca)$. KEA's key credits 0 (see note on the angle values).

questions.q: The modulus of the complex number $\dfrac{(1+i)^2(1+3i)}{(2-6i)(2-2i)}$ is
questions.explanation: $(1+i)^2=2i$, numerator $=2i(1+3i)=-6+2i$ with modulus $2\sqrt{10}$; denominator $=(2-6i)(2-2i)=-8-16i$ with modulus $8\sqrt5$. Ratio $=\dfrac{2\sqrt{10}}{8\sqrt5}=\dfrac{\sqrt2}{4}$.

questions.q: Given that a, b and x are real numbers and $a < b, x < 0$ then
questions.explanation: Dividing $a<b$ by a negative number $x$ reverses the inequality: $a/x > b/x$.

questions.q: Ten chairs are numbered as 1 to 10. Three women and two men wish to occupy one chair each. First the women choose the chairs marked 1 to 6, then the men choose the chairs from the remaining. The number of possible ways is
questions.explanation: Women arrange in 3 of the 6 chairs: $^6P_3$ ways; men then arrange in 2 of the remaining 4 chairs (7-10): $^4P_2$ ways. Total $=\,{}^6P_3\times{}^4P_2$.

questions.q: Which of the following is an empty set?
questions.explanation: $x^2+1=0$ has no real solutions, so this set is empty; the others each have real solutions ($\pm3$, $\pm1$, and $2,-1$ respectively).
